#CURRENCIES IN COLLAPSE: THE GLOBAL DOLLAR DOMINANCE

As the greenback surges, the rest of the world is feeling the burn. One war. Thirteen currencies on fire. The dollar wins—everyone else pays the price.

The Front Lines: Total Freefall

Iran (﷼): Down over 30%. The Rial has plummeted from 1.35M to 1.75M per USD. A total currency freefall.

Turkey (₺): The central bank burned $12 BILLION in a single week just to break the fall. It’s still sliding.
Egypt (£): Smashed to a record low of 52.8 per dollar.
Asia & Emerging Markets: The New Laggards

South Korea (₩): The top laggard in Asia, dropping 1.67% in a single day.

Indonesia (Rp): Slipped from 16,760 to 16,868/USD since the conflict began—and the floor is nowhere in sight.
Thailand (฿) & Philippines (₱): Massive single-day plunges. The Philippine central bank has been forced to abandon planned rate cuts to defend the Peso.
India (₹): Fell past 91/USD, marking its weakest performance in a month.
Commodities & Regional Volatility

Chile ($): With copper crashing 8%, the Peso is being dragged into the dirt.

Brazil (R$): Leading the bleeding across Latin American markets.
South Africa (R): Ranked as one of the worst-performing Emerging Market currencies since late February.
Poland (zł): Downgraded by JPMorgan as CEE currencies face extreme exposure.
Societal Breaking Points

Pakistan (₨): Fuel prices skyrocketed 20% in one week. The crisis is so severe that schools have closed and a four-day work week has been implemented to conserve energy.

The Bottom Line: We are witnessing a global realignment. When the dollar weaponizes, the world’s most vulnerable economies are the first to fracture.

LOOK: Philippine National Police (PNP) personnel from the Muntinlupa City Police Station conduct bicycle patrols along the main road in Barangay Tunasan, Muntinlupa City on Wednesday, March 11.

The initiative is part of the PNP’s efforts to conserve fuel amid concerns over a looming oil crisis linked to ongoing tensions in the Middle East. Authorities say the move also helps maintain police visibility and allows officers to better navigate traffic and narrow streets in communities.

📷: Mark Balmores | MB
